boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named University of Georgia spaces for studying, collaborating, creating, gathering, reflecting, and attending films.

cards.title: Tate Student Center
cards.subtitle: 45 Baxter Street · central campus
cards.notes: Use Tate as a central meet-up point: choose a lounge or open space to study, play a game, or catch up before heading to your next stop.
cards.short_summary: A campus hub with lounges, games, events, and student-facing services.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA describes Tate as a daily gathering place where people can sit, play games, study, and catch up with friends.
cards.access_notes: Programming and individual spaces may have separate hours or reservation rules; check Tate before an event.

cards.title: South Lawn
cards.subtitle: Tate Student Center · 45 Baxter Street
cards.notes: Bring a chair or blanket for an outdoor study break, then use the lawn to catch up with classmates between activities at Tate.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor Tate space intended for studying or spending time with friends.
cards.evidence_claim: Tate identifies South Lawn as a space to pull up a chair, study, or catch up with friends.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor conditions and campus programming can affect use; follow posted event and space-reservation guidance.

cards.title: Reflection Room
cards.subtitle: Third floor · Tate Student Center
cards.notes: Head to the third floor when you need a quiet pause; use the room for individual meditation or reflection rather than a group meetup.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, meditative room within Tate.
cards.evidence_claim: Tate directs visitors to its third-floor Reflection Room for a quiet, meditative space.
cards.access_notes: Use quietly and check Tate for any room-specific availability guidance.

cards.title: Tate Theatre
cards.subtitle: Tate Student Center · 45 Baxter Street
cards.notes: Check the Tate movie schedule, bring your own food if desired, and plan a film outing in the student center rather than leaving campus.
cards.short_summary: A campus theatre that hosts films with free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: Tate states that Tate Theatre offers free admission and allows guests to bring their own food for films.
cards.access_notes: See Tate’s movie schedule for showtimes and any event-specific guidance.

cards.title: Miller Learning Center
cards.subtitle: 48 Baxter Street · 2nd–4th floors
cards.notes: Use the floor screens or UGA app to locate an available group room, then settle in at a table for individual or collaborative work.
cards.short_summary: A large academic building with group rooms, study tables, computers, and support services.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA Libraries lists 95 first-come, first-served MLC group study rooms and study tables on floors 2–4.
cards.access_notes: UGA or other college ID is required after 9 p.m.; group rooms are first-come, first-served.

cards.title: Sidney Samuel Thomas Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Third floor · Miller Learning Center
cards.notes: Choose this third-floor room for quiet reading or focused work, and keep group discussion for the MLC’s other collaborative areas.
cards.short_summary: A quiet MLC reading room with seating for up to 100 people.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA Libraries identifies the third-floor Sidney Samuel Thomas Reading Room as a quiet study space with a maximum capacity of 100.
cards.access_notes: Located on MLC’s third floor; observe quiet-study expectations and building access rules.

cards.title: Creative Engagement Wing
cards.subtitle: Third floor · Miller Learning Center
cards.notes: Visit the third floor to explore hands-on project tools, practice a presentation, or ask about creating audio, video, VR, or maker work.
cards.short_summary: A technology-rich MLC wing for collaborative and hands-on learning.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA says the Creative Engagement Wing facilitates student collaboration, hands-on learning, and work with tools including 3D printing and media production.
cards.access_notes: Located on the MLC third floor; tool use, consultations, and specialized spaces may have separate procedures.

cards.title: Collaborative Study Space
cards.subtitle: Fourth floor · Main Library
cards.notes: Bring a small group to the fourth floor to discuss coursework and use the whiteboard walls or chalkboard columns to work through ideas.
cards.short_summary: A Main Library space designed for groups to meet and discuss.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA Libraries says the Main Library’s fourth-floor Collaborative Study Space has seating for groups, whiteboard walls, and chalkboard columns.
cards.access_notes: Main Library requires a UGA or other college ID after 6 p.m.; check current building hours before visiting.

cards.title: Barr Seminar Room
cards.subtitle: First floor · Main Library
cards.notes: Reserve this room when your group needs a monitor, movable tables, and a whiteboard; schedule only the time you need for the session.
cards.short_summary: A reservable Main Library room for groups of up to 12.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA Libraries states that the Barr Seminar Room accommodates groups of up to 12 and can be reserved in 30-minute increments for up to four hours daily.
cards.access_notes: Reserve online; the source limits reservations to a maximum of four hours per day.

cards.title: McBay Science Library
cards.subtitle: 210 D.W. Brooks Drive · South Campus
cards.notes: Use McBay’s open seating for a study session or discussion, and check the UGA app if your group needs one of the fourth-floor rooms.
cards.short_summary: A South Campus library with study seating, study booths, and group rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: UGA Libraries lists open study seating and 25 small group study rooms on McBay Science Library’s fourth floor.
cards.access_notes: UGA or other college ID is required after 6 p.m.; availability for fourth-floor group rooms is provided through the UGA app.
